title: Autonomy with a mandate and a memory

speaker: Dinis Cruz

beats.title: Title
beats.cue: 7:00 pm, first of three community talks; rUv's keynote was at 6:00. Livestreamed to YouTube.

slide.kicker: Agentic Engineering Live · rUv in London
slide.text: Autonomy with a mandate and a memory
slide.sub: sgit vaults and Agent Behaviour Policies, running inside rUv's stack

beats.say: I'm Dinis. I build sgit, git for encrypted vaults, and Agent Behaviour Policies. Ten minutes; everything on screen comes from a recorded run, and the site and the vault are public.

beats.title: The claim

slide.text: Autonomy needs two more things to be trusted.

builds.text: Memory with history the host can't read.

beats.say: rUv's stack lets agents go to town: swarms, consensus, self-learning. Autonomy needs two more things to be trusted: a written mandate per agent, and memory with history the host can't read. Tonight both run inside his tools.

beats.title: rUv's stack, one picture

slide.caption: Bottom to top: RVM, RuVector, Ruflo, MetaHarness, the hosts. All MIT, by rUv / ruvnet.

beats.say: His stack, bottom up: RVM, the capability VM; RuVector, the memory; Ruflo, the orchestrator, with queens and eight worker roles; MetaHarness, which assembles a harness for a host; and the hosts you already use. It's overwhelming because it's complete. I plug into two places: Ruflo's policy engine, and the memory.

beats.title: Ruflo's default

slide.caption: Recorded 14 Oct 2026 · ruflo 3.56.10, fresh project · evidence/ruflo-policy-legacy.json

beats.say: Ruflo has a real policy engine: rules, budgets, a hash-chained receipt ledger. But on a fresh project its mode is legacy. Ask whether the coder may send email: allowed, legacy-default-allow. Nobody wrote down that it may not, so it may.

beats.title: What a mandate looks like

slide.caption: One role of the ABP: the coder

beats.say: This is the mandate: an Agent Behaviour Policy. One row per capability, in a grammar: verb, object, reach. Is it mandated, why, and the barrier when it isn't. Agents draft, a person sends: so send dot message dot world is no, with a policy deny and no mail credential. Six roles, 36 rows, zero gaps; a gap is reach with no mandate and no barrier, and in CI a gap fails the build.

beats.title: Same 11 actions, default against the ABP
beats.cue: Rows reveal every 5 s; the stopped ones are the point.

slide.caption: Same 11 actions: Ruflo's default against the ABP

beats.say: Compile the ABP into Ruflo's own engine and play the same eleven actions twice. Left, the default: everything allowed. Right, enforce mode with the ABP: email denied, pastebin denied, the tester editing source denied, the researcher reading AWS credentials denied; the push and the deploy need a named human. Six of eleven stopped, five allowed, and every reason names its ABP row. Your engine enforces it. The ABP is the mandate it enforces.

beats.title: Ask the mandate, in the browser
beats.cue: Live page; it types the question itself. Esc returns the keyboard if you click into it.

slide.caption: The live app: RuVector WASM in the browser, ABP rows indexed, offline after load. Also served from the public vault.

beats.say: The same mandate in the browser. This page loads RuVector's WASM build, indexes the 36 ABP rows, and answers offline. Can the coder send email? No: agents draft, a person sends; the barrier is right there, with the owner and the expiry date.

beats.title: Every decision is a receipt
beats.say: And every decision is a receipt: hash-chained, each one pointing at the previous, and the ledger verifies. Eleven each side, both valid. That's evidence an auditor, or the next agent, can check.

beats.title: Memory: the gap

slide.text: What the memory layer doesn't do yet

builds.text: no encryption at rest or in transit
“collections and metadata filters … are not a complete authorization boundary”

beats.say: Second half: memory. RuVector is a remarkable memory substrate, and its README is honest about what it doesn't do yet: no encryption at rest or in transit, no document versioning, and collections are not a complete authorization boundary. That is exactly the layer sgit is.

beats.title: Memory with history

slide.caption: POC2, recorded 14 Oct 2026 · ruflo 3.56.10 · sgit-ai 0.21.0 · evidence/poc2-run.txt
slide.output:
3bf90dd8d00a (HEAD)  memory: tester learned something in run local-20261014T2132  +5  [blobs:+5 trees:+3]
8ac2a0e9f200  memory: coder learned something in run local-20261014T2132  +5  [blobs:+5 trees:+4]
1ac3298a6cc9  init: memory vault  +1  [blobs:+1]
48aaaee48630  init

# fresh clone, DB files restored, ruflo memory list -n <role>:
== coder
| coder/lesson-local-202... | coder     | 72 B |   -    |        0 | 4m ago  |
[INFO] Showing 1 of 1 entries
== tester
| tester/lesson-local-20... | tester    | 72 B |   -    |        0 | 4m ago  |
[INFO] Showing 1 of 1 entries

beats.say: Each agent role writes its Ruflo memory on its own branch of a vault, encrypted on the client, AES-256-GCM; the server only sees ciphertext. The branches merge. Then the folder is deleted, the vault cloned fresh, the memory restored, and Ruflo asked again: coder and tester answer as before. The history says who learned what, and when.

beats.title: Rights compiled from the mandate

slide.caption: RVM capability rights, compiled from the same ABP
slide.footer: 0 gaps · EXECUTE covers a test run and an email send alike; the ABP keeps the difference · source: data/rvm-caps.md

beats.say: One more compile target: RVM, his capability VM. The same rows become capability token rights per role. Tokens are coarser than the mandate: EXECUTE covers a test run and an email send alike. So compile the tokens from the mandate, and keep the why.

beats.title: Where it runs

slide.kicker: Six POCs · status as on ruv.sgit.ai/pocs.html
items: CI: ABP gate, POC1, POC3, POC5 on every push; publishing waits for a named human
Browser: RuVector WASM, page served from a public sgit vault
MetaHarness: its scaffold rendered as an ABP and diffed against ours
Claude Code + Ruflo as MCP: a runbook; policy admin needs a human at the terminal

beats.say: Where it runs: in CI, where the ABP is a test and publishing waits for a named human; in the browser, from a vault; against MetaHarness, whose scaffold we read as an ABP and diffed. The Claude Code session is a runbook: Ruflo's policy admin wants a human at an interactive terminal, and we did not work around that.

beats.title: The ask

slide.text: Pick one, and we build it together.

builds.text: Ruflo policy profiles generated from ABPs
…and show it back here, at a future Agentics London.

beats.say: So, the ask. Pick one, and we build it together: Ruflo policy profiles generated from ABPs, so a swarm ships with its mandate; or vault-backed memory for RuVector, encrypted, versioned, branch per agent. And we show it back here, at a future Agentics London.
